## P1 - sharpens-framing: retain the timeout pain, separate diagnosis from fallback text

Evidence: [release/constants.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/5aac3ef3f8d0bd818bec862bba6b56391bfa9884/packages/core/src/release/constants.ts) fixes the wall cap at 60 minutes. [ts-check-lane/run-lane.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/5aac3ef3f8d0bd818bec862bba6b56391bfa9884/packages/core/src/ts-check-lane/run-lane.ts) uses that environment to select vitest WITHOUT coverage. Local coverage-final.json is therefore not an expected success artifact for the normal pinned Step 5 path. The pipeline's missing-report diagnostic does not establish a coverage merge hang.

Failure mode: treating the missing JSON or last completed chronology.test.ts as the causal unit selects the wrong remediation. [progress-reporter.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/5aac3ef3f8d0bd818bec862bba6b56391bfa9884/packages/core/src/ts-check-lane/progress-reporter.ts) records last-file at module completion and separately tracks in-flight modules. A completed file is not the unfinished offender; the whole Step 5 deadline also includes work outside that file.

Consequence: preserve P1 as a reported Step 5 timeout, but require actual lane argv/coverage condition and phase/in-flight evidence before binding a root-cause claim. The discrepancy could reflect incident-version behavior or diagnostic fallback; this pin-read does not refute the incident log.

Consequence: name the incremental change beyond these mechanisms and its measured delta. Reject a detector-only raise as the durable sole remedy under this Stop 1. Evidence: [skip-ci-incident.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/5aac3ef3f8d0bd818bec862bba6b56391bfa9884/packages/core/src/release/skip-ci-incident.ts) accepts a numeric incident citation and prints a next-production-patch warning; validateSkipCiIncident receives no release-version scope and does not check that the cited incident authorizes that version. A new authorization subsystem is not needed to diagnose this hang; if a proposed Bound claims mechanical prevention of reuse, it must add and test version binding rather than rely on the existing warning.

## P4 - blocks-the-design: a cheaper subset or cached Step 5 is not proof of full-path recovery

Evidence: runReleaseCheck requires the suite to have run and a successful tip-SHA GHA coverage-of-record cite. [release/pipeline.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/5aac3ef3f8d0bd818bec862bba6b56391bfa9884/packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts) also has a clean-HEAD suite-stamp path that can report Step 5 OK while skipping the suite. A targeted chronology test, a warm stamp hit, or a Linux coverage job can all pass without measuring the Windows full-check wall-clock that P1 names.

Failure mode: binding relief from one of those proxies repeats the unproven sub-60-minute residual. A follow-on issue being filed, without a landed change and measurement, likewise does not meet Stop 1's alternative.

Consequence: do not bind a remedy with only subset timing or a generic green Step 5 label. The evidence path must distinguish an actual full run from a stamp hit and include the Windows host, tested SHA, resolved command/environment, tool versions, cold/warm state, worker/project configuration, file census, phase times, full Step 5 elapsed time and exit status, absence of skip-ci, and the tip-SHA GHA coverage cite. A focused rerun is diagnostic evidence, not the acceptance oracle. The existing #5140 overlap and share-plus-reset decisions make that a concrete constraint, not a reason to serialize the whole suite by default.

Road not taken: another cap increase is the smallest implementation and could be appropriate for demonstrably healthy necessary work whose accepted latency changed. It is not supported here as the sole durable remedy. No lean is posted; these are findings for parent disposition.

### F1 -- the no-coverage decline branch is unreachable in production, and its guard test proves the wrong thing

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** `formatSuiteBoundCoverageDecline` calls `suiteExpectedToWriteLocalCoverage(reason)` with the default env argument, so it reads the **release parent's** `process.env`. But `RELEASE_PREFLIGHT_ENV` is never set on that parent: `releaseCheckEnv()` (`packages/core/src/release/preflight.ts:39-57`) builds a *separate* env object carrying `[RELEASE_PREFLIGHT_ENV]: "1"` and hands it to the Step 5 child, while `releaseSubprocessEnv()` (`packages/core/src/release/git.ts:10`) sets only the two `DEFT_ALLOW_*` keys. I did not, because the 1314/1334 to 153/1366 delta across 48 hours and 32 added specs cannot be produced by suite composition, and binding cheapen first spends the arc on a real but secondary problem while the primary one stays unnamed. Cheapen belongs in the Bound; it is not the first step.
